about:
Today I heard the air conditioner turn off for the first time in months. August 28th, low of 73 degrees. A miracle in Austin, TX.

It must have been fall when I recorded Way I Do, because my air conditioner was turning on and off the way it does when things finally cool down. I know this because it's part of the song. The first time was an accident. Perfectly timed with the climax. After that, it was very much on purpose.

My studio is small but mighty. Cables criss cross every surface. Five guitars hang on the right wall, three keyboards to the left. And behind me is the drum set, facing into the corner with a little mirror so everyone can still see each other when we rehearse.

I pointed my mic at the vent and opened the studio door. Down the hall, I found the thermostat, cranked it down and clicked the switch from "off" to "cool". My instrument. I held my breath as the ancient ductwork rumbled to life beneath my feet.

I made "i'm not scared now" in an expensive studio. In a place like that, they turn the AC off during each take. Every minute costs money, and you have to come prepared. But I wanted to explore. I love writing in the studio, capturing the moment of discovery on tape. Stumbling towards an idea, getting closer with each grasping take. When it finally lands, I'm hearing it for the first time, just like you.

So I made Way I Do at home.

The lyrics are about living with my partner and developing a crush on our roommate. Crushes are normal, even when you're with someone. They don't have to threaten the relationship, especially if you talk about it. But having her in the house felt dangerous. Like it could fuck up my whole life. When she moved out, it was like hearing that air conditioner finally turning off.

I left that situation stronger. I proved to myself that I'm in control, that my feelings don't call the shots. This might sound backwards, but I have depression. My feelings are dirty little liars sometimes. They tell me the worst things about myself and the world, and I used to believe them. I can't control my feelings, but I can control my choices. And I'm not scared of them anymore.

If Tumble taught me what Elliot.wavs sounds like, then Way I Do gave me the confidence to make that sound with my own two hands.
